origin: TMM original quests informed by ATM10 structure; no copied quest prose

rules.each_quest_requires: Positive XP and meaningful items/approved coins except narrowly scoped Ars orientation, which gives five XP only.
rules.reward_shortcuts: no fixed item reward equals another authored item criterion; shop purchases intentionally bypass bad-luck but cannot bypass progression locks
rules.criteria_reuse: never duplicate an objective by accident; the six explicitly designated copper/emerald/diamond sell-tier item IDs are intentionally reused with different counts and item consumption
rules.overview_placeholders: until authored, minimal paper + XP checkmark rewards
rules.progression_chapters: 56 authored progression quests; Skills & Factions replaces stale Pufferfish skill guidance and owns class and transformation orientation.
rules.onboarding: Seven added Getting Started quests beyond iron, guiding first spell/ritual and exploration; no specific magical school required.
rules.new_tips: Four optional practical Tips: Scriptor fuel-free automatic smelting, Occultism/Mahou ore processing, broom alternatives, and Vengeance Pickaxe.
rules.ars_pilot: 49 completed Ars quests from manifest/ars_quest_pilot.json; no auto-claim and 48 substantive item rewards; current Welcome and Punch a Tree retain all starter items.

quests.title: Welcome to Too Much Magic
quests.description: A magic-first modpack with many independent schools. Introduction gives you the essentials, Progression connects systems, and the other groups guide individual mods. Check this welcome entry to claim an Unwitnessed Amulet and a Ring of the Seven Curses. Equipping the cursed ring is optional and has significant drawbacks.

quests.title: Choose Your Magic Controls
quests.description: Too Much Magic keeps Minecraft's normal movement, combat, and inventory controls. For a fresh player, mod-added keybindings are intended to start unbound so dozens of mods cannot silently fight over shortcuts. Open Options > Controls > Key Binds to assign only the magic and utility actions you want. Controlling helps find bindings and conflicts. Your changes are personal; this quest does not reset anything. KeySets is included for one test build and may be removed if its controls or saved profiles prove unreliable.

quests.title: I'm Ready for Regular Mode
quests.description: New players begin in Newbie Mode, with protected inventory/experience and convenience travel, but without MXP or faction enrollment. When YOU are ready for full survival progression, check this box and claim your personal graduation reward. This permanently enables Regular Mode for your character: normal death and Corail graves, no home/rtp/back, MXP and class enrollment. Graduation is one-way without an administrator. In a team, each player must claim their own reward; never force graduation on teammates.

quests.title: Punch a Tree
quests.description: Pick up any log or stem to complete this quest, then claim a 27-slot Trinkets Pouch and 10 XP. No hidden advancement or automatic item delivery is used. Do not place portable bags inside other bags; cross-mod enforcement is still in development.

quests.title: Make a Crafting Table
quests.description: Craft a table to unlock the familiar 3x3 crafting grid. It is a useful baseline before you explore magical crafting.

quests.title: Make a Wooden Pickaxe
quests.description: Craft your first wooden pickaxe. Ordinary tools are an easy way to get established before specializing in magic.

quests.title: Gather Stone
quests.description: Collect sixteen cobblestone. Stone is useful for your first shelter, tools and furnace.

quests.title: Upgrade to Stone
quests.description: Make a stone pickaxe so you can mine sturdier resources.

quests.title: A Place for Your Things
quests.description: Craft a chest for early base storage. Magic eventually offers more specialized options than generic storage networks.

quests.title: Light the Furnace
quests.description: Craft a furnace. Smelting remains useful alongside later magical processing.

quests.title: Find Your First Iron
quests.description: Bring back three raw iron. Magical mining and transmutation will eventually provide alternatives.

quests.title: Iron Pickaxe
quests.description: Craft an iron pickaxe. You now have the baseline tools to choose your first magical specialty.

quests.title: Begin a Library
quests.description: Craft a book to begin collecting magical research and manuals. Akashic Tome can organize compatible guides without replacing each school's progression.

quests.title: Tips & Tricks Index
quests.description: These optional read-and-check tips cover tools, keys and systems that a large modpack makes easy to overlook. The tips are not compulsory progression gates.

quests.title: Find Recipes with JEI
quests.description: Use Just Enough Items to explore recipes and item usages. Check both directions before assuming a resource has only one way to obtain it.

quests.title: Identify Blocks with Jade
quests.description: Jade identifies blocks and creatures under your crosshair and can display useful supported-mod information.

quests.title: Sort Your Inventory
quests.description: Inventory Tweaks ReFoxed provides inventory sorting and refill features. Middle-click sorting depends on key bindings and the container; Mouse Tweaks also changes dragging and scrolling.

quests.title: Use Crafting Tweaks
quests.description: Crafting Tweaks can rotate, balance or clear a normal crafting grid. Test those controls before assuming they work in a modded ritual interface.

quests.title: Search the Controls Screen
quests.description: Use the controls search to find conflicting mod keys. KeyBind Bundles can help organize different play styles.

quests.title: Gather Your Guidebooks
quests.description: Akashic Tome can collect compatible magic manuals into one book. Not every guide is compatible and you may need to acquire some books individually.

quests.title: Curios and Portable Bags
quests.description: Curios provides extra equipment slots. Never nest portable bags: Ars Elemental has a partial blacklist, but Occultism and ProjectE require more complete safeguards before survival release.

quests.title: Claim Your Base
quests.description: Use FTB Chunks to claim an area around your base. Chunk loading depends on server settings; protection and backups solve different problems.

quests.title: Understand Lootr Chests
quests.description: Lootr supports per-player loot in many generated chests. Exact behavior can depend on the structure and container.

quests.title: Plan for Death
quests.description: Corail Tombstone changes recovery after death. Learn how graves work before a dangerous expedition, and keep backups while death-handler compatibility is under review.

quests.title: Search Biomes
quests.description: Nature's Compass can locate biomes relevant to exploration and magic. It is not a Waystone or teleport system.

quests.title: Resolve Recipe Conflicts
quests.description: Polymorph can help when multiple recipes have the same ingredients. Check the intended output before spending scarce materials.

quests.title: Understand Character Growth
quests.description: Core Magic (Tyz's Skills) and ordinary-experience Improvable Skills 3 are available to everyone in Regular Mode. Specializations use a single exclusive choice pool with only explicit exceptions; see Skills & Factions.

quests.title: Zoom and Overlay Controls
quests.description: Just Zoom and More Overlays Updated offer visual aids. Adjust key bindings if they conflict with other mod controls.

quests.title: Food & Fishing Index
quests.description: Farming, fishing and cooking offer useful alternatives to combat foraging. Explore these branches independently and use JEI for the many additional Pam's HarvestCraft recipes.

quests.title: Start with Seeds
quests.description: Collect wheat seeds to start a farm. The installed food mods offer many additional crops as you explore.

quests.title: Prepare a Field
quests.description: Craft a stone hoe to till farmland. Harvest with Ease can make managing mature crops simpler.

quests.title: Bring in the Wheat
quests.description: Harvest four wheat. Ordinary grains form a foundation for many more elaborate meals.

quests.title: A Patch of Sugar Cane
quests.description: Collect three sugar cane. Sugar and paper support cooking and magic books.

quests.title: Raise a Chicken Dinner
quests.description: Acquire raw chicken. Farmer's Delight and Pam's HarvestCraft offer cooking options beyond simple smelting.

quests.title: Gather Eggs
quests.description: Collect two eggs for cooking recipes.

quests.title: Fresh Milk
quests.description: Get a bucket of milk. Many recipes need useful basic farm products as well as exotic ingredients.

quests.title: Ready Your Fishing Rod
quests.description: Craft a fishing rod and start exploring another renewable food route.

quests.title: Catch a Cod
quests.description: Catch cod using a rod. A small fishing expedition can feed a player before a serious farm is built.

quests.title: Catch a Salmon
quests.description: Catch salmon in suitable water. Aquaculture expands this side of the game.

quests.title: Aquaculture: Iron Rod
quests.description: Craft Aquaculture 2's iron fishing rod. Use JEI for its current exact recipe.

quests.title: Aquaculture: Gold Rod
quests.description: Progress to an Aquaculture gold fishing rod. This is a distinct milestone, not another copy of the iron-rod objective.

quests.title: Aquaculture: Neptunium Rod
quests.description: Obtain the rare Neptunium fishing rod as an optional long-term goal rather than an early prerequisite.

quests.title: Light a Campfire
quests.description: Craft a campfire to cook basic food on the road.

quests.title: Farmer's Delight: Cutting Board
quests.description: Craft Farmer's Delight's cutting board to prepare ingredients outside the normal crafting grid.

quests.title: Farmer's Delight: Cooking Pot
quests.description: Make a cooking pot and use it with heat and ingredients for more satisfying meals.

quests.title: Find the Seed Market
quests.description: Craft Farming for Blockheads' Market for ordinary seed and sapling trades. Magical seed trades must be audited before survival release.

quests.title: Pam's HarvestCraft: Fried Chicken
quests.description: Craft a finished Fried Chicken from Pam's HarvestCraft 2 Food Core. A useful optional cooking challenge.

quests.title: Pam's HarvestCraft: Starfruit
quests.description: Obtain starfruit from Pam's HarvestCraft 2 Trees, showcasing specialty plants and orchard progression.

quests.title: Use the Quest Shop
quests.description: Use /hqs shop to browse a curated list of convenience supplies, common magical materials, exploration finds, and specific Artifacts. Quest Shop coins belong to your FTB Team. Ordinary quests generally give thematic item rewards; specialized resource-selling quests pay coins.

quests.title: Cooking for Blockheads: Cooking Table
quests.description: Build the Cooking Table to discover dishes available from nearby kitchen ingredients. Cooking for Blockheads works alongside Farmer's Delight and Pam's HarvestCraft, expanding an organized base kitchen.

quests.title: Cooking for Blockheads: Oven
quests.description: Build an Oven to expand the modular kitchen. Check recipes and heating behavior in JEI and test compatibility with food ingredients before automating the kitchen.

quests.title: Sell Copper I — First Trade
quests.description: Submit 8 pieces of copper as a one-time sale. The exchange consumes the materials and credits your team's Quest Shop balance with one coin. Later tiers require larger deliveries.

quests.title: Sell Copper II — Regular Buyer
quests.description: Submit 32 pieces of copper as a one-time sale. The exchange consumes the materials and credits your team's Quest Shop balance with one coin. Later tiers require larger deliveries.

quests.title: Sell Copper III — Packed Shipment
quests.description: Submit 16 blocks of copper as a one-time sale. The exchange consumes the materials and credits your team's Quest Shop balance with one coin. Later tiers require larger deliveries.

quests.title: Sell Copper IV — Industrial Exchange
quests.description: Repeatable bulk sale: submit 256 full copper blocks (4 stacks) for a single coin. The items must be consumed. After ProjectE unlocks, manufacturing large quantities for shop currency is an intended late-game option.

quests.title: Sell Emeralds I — First Trade
quests.description: Submit 2 pieces of emeralds as a one-time sale. The exchange consumes the materials and credits your team's Quest Shop balance with one coin. Later tiers require larger deliveries.

quests.title: Sell Emeralds II — Regular Buyer
quests.description: Submit 8 pieces of emeralds as a one-time sale. The exchange consumes the materials and credits your team's Quest Shop balance with one coin. Later tiers require larger deliveries.

quests.title: Sell Emeralds III — Packed Shipment
quests.description: Submit 16 blocks of emeralds as a one-time sale. The exchange consumes the materials and credits your team's Quest Shop balance with one coin. Later tiers require larger deliveries.

quests.title: Sell Emeralds IV — Industrial Exchange
quests.description: Repeatable bulk sale: submit 128 full emeralds blocks (2 stacks) for a single coin. The items must be consumed. After ProjectE unlocks, manufacturing large quantities for shop currency is an intended late-game option.

quests.title: Sell Diamonds I — First Trade
quests.description: Submit 1 pieces of diamonds as a one-time sale. The exchange consumes the materials and credits your team's Quest Shop balance with one coin. Later tiers require larger deliveries.

quests.title: Sell Diamonds II — Regular Buyer
quests.description: Submit 4 pieces of diamonds as a one-time sale. The exchange consumes the materials and credits your team's Quest Shop balance with one coin. Later tiers require larger deliveries.

quests.title: Sell Diamonds III — Packed Shipment
quests.description: Submit 8 blocks of diamonds as a one-time sale. The exchange consumes the materials and credits your team's Quest Shop balance with one coin. Later tiers require larger deliveries.

quests.title: Sell Diamonds IV — Industrial Exchange
quests.description: Repeatable bulk sale: submit 64 full diamonds blocks (1 stack) for a single coin. The items must be consumed. After ProjectE unlocks, manufacturing large quantities for shop currency is an intended late-game option.

quests.title: Choose a Magical Tradition
quests.description: Pick one school of magic that interests you, then open its own chapter. Ars Nouveau, Occultism, Botania, Hex Casting, and the other traditions can be explored in parallel. This is a guide checkmark, not a mandatory choice or a gate on the other chapters.

quests.title: Secure Some Copper
quests.description: Bring back eight raw copper. Copper supports the world's ordinary utility blocks as well as several magical crafts. The separate coin-exchange branch consumes processed copper; gathering raw ore here is a distinct objective.

quests.title: Prospect for Gold
quests.description: Find four raw gold. Gold is useful for redstone infrastructure, enchantment-related crafting and many magical ingredients.

quests.title: Learn to Recognize Lapis
quests.description: Bring eight lapis lazuli. It supports enchantment and an assortment of magical recipes; JEI shows the exact uses in this pack.

quests.title: Collect Amethyst
quests.description: Collect eight amethyst shards, or buy them from Quest Shop if the geology refuses to cooperate. A purchased ingredient is an intentional anti-grind alternative, not a bypass of any late-game boss gate.

quests.title: Bring a Water Bucket
quests.description: Keep water accessible for building, agriculture, and many magical structures. This milestone is separate from Food & Fishing's milk-bucket quest.

quests.title: Defend Yourself
quests.description: Make a shield. Early defensive options make it easier to travel while discovering spells and supernatural equipment.

quests.title: Upgrade to Diamond Mining
quests.description: Craft a diamond pickaxe when you are ready to move beyond iron. It is a practical exploration baseline, not a requirement to pursue all magic schools.

quests.title: Reach the Nether for Ingredients
quests.description: Acquire a blaze rod in the Nether. The Nether is one of several routes toward stronger magical ingredients and more dangerous encounters; this objective does not duplicate a specialist chapter's spellcasting milestone.

quests.title: Gather Ender Pearls
quests.description: Collect four ender pearls. They support teleportation, several magical recipes and preparation for eventual End exploration.

quests.title: Map Out Your Infrastructure
quests.description: A developed magical base benefits from a few focused work areas: enchanting and potions, ritual floors, stable item storage, and safe power machinery. Many schools are independent; there is no mandatory universal industrial network.

quests.title: Install an Enchanting Table
quests.description: Craft an enchanting table, add bookshelves when convenient, and compare enchantments to spellcasting upgrades. Apotheosis has deeper enchantment mechanics in its own chapter.

quests.title: Bring an Anvil
quests.description: Craft an anvil for conventional repairs, naming, and combining compatible enchantments. This supplements magical equipment rather than replacing its unique upgrades.

quests.title: Build a Brewing Stand
quests.description: Craft a brewing stand and explore potion recipes. Potion and herb-based systems also have specialized paths in Witchcraft, Hexerei and other chapters.

quests.title: Build a Portal Reserve
quests.description: Bring ten obsidian for a safe portal or important construction work. Consider well-lit, protected portal sites; dimensions remain separate exploration branches.

quests.title: Keep an Ender Chest
quests.description: Craft an Ender Chest for vanilla portable access to a personal inventory. Occultism remains the pack's featured expandable magical storage path, and generic item logistics networks remain excluded.

quests.title: Recover Ancient Debris Products
quests.description: Acquire one Netherite Scrap to introduce late-game conventional material upgrades. This does not unlock boss-gated draconium or Replication materials.

quests.title: Construct a Lodestone
quests.description: Craft a lodestone and use it with a compass as a reliable base or remote-site landmark. The pack deliberately does not include Waystones.

quests.title: Understand Summoning Rituals
quests.description: Summoning Rituals is a custom recipe framework: it does not bring a complete fixed questline of ritual recipes by default. Check JEI and the TMM recipe registry for any implemented pack-specific offerings. Do not assume speculative rituals work until authored and tested.

quests.title: Prepare a Protected Ritual Chamber
quests.description: Reserve sufficient space for multiblocks, separate hazardous machinery, and keep vulnerable farms and storage away from explosive experiments. This is a planning checkmark, not an automated claim that a structure exists.

quests.title: Roadmap: Read Before the Endgame
quests.description: This is a reference page, not another boss checklist. The Endgame category owns the actual Draconic Evolution, ProjectE and Replication quests, while Cataclysm and Occultism own their own unique milestones. Mark this read when you understand the links.

quests.title: Roadmap: The End and Draconic Materials
quests.description: The End is a major progression junction: dragon encounters, dangerous exploration and draconium resources. The precise uranium and draconic-dust generation restrictions are still under design; the questbook cannot enforce a pending ore-generation rule.

quests.title: Roadmap: Cataclysm Boss Resources
quests.description: The Harbinger and Ignis are proposed sources for late Eldritch Ancient Miner requirements. Their exact rewards and material keys must be verified in the installed Cataclysm version; this page does not grant boss loot or mark either boss defeated.

quests.title: Roadmap: Occultism's Final Miner
quests.description: The Eldritch Ancient Miner is intended to offer a difficult renewable Replication ore route. The proposed cost is two to four Marid-tier components plus high-level boss materials, possibly late Botania; none of these recipe changes is assumed implemented.

quests.title: Roadmap: Chaos Guardian as the Gate
quests.description: Defeating the Chaos Guardian must precede every usable ProjectE and Project Expansion acquisition or function. This is a rule for actual gameplay enforcement, not something a checked roadmap page can unlock. The boss objective belongs to Draconic Evolution's Endgame chapter.

quests.title: Roadmap: What Unlocks Afterwards
quests.description: After verified Chaos Guardian completion, pursue the ProjectE and Project Expansion progression, Gem Armor and other genuinely late options. Replication and its miner route remain a separate arc. Re:Avaritia, Extended Crafting and the Ring of the Seven Deadly Sins are excluded.

quests.title: Read the Two Skill Systems
quests.description: Every character has access to Core Magic through Tyz's Skills in Regular Mode. Core is universal and does not occupy a specialization slot. Improvable Skills 3 uses ordinary experience separately and is also available to everyone. Graduate from Newbie Mode before earning MXP or joining a faction.

quests.title: Open the Skill Interface
quests.description: Assign the Tyz's Skills key in Options > Controls > Key Binds and open the skill interface. Core Magic is the universal tree; any additional specialization is contingent on enrollment or native form acquisition. Available trees and effects depend on current integrated data. This is orientation, not proof of a purchase.

quests.title: Understand Attributes
quests.description: Inspect displayed skill effects and relevant attributes. Pufferfish Attributes is a supporting library, not the player skill tree. Damage, resource efficiency and cooldown hooks differ by magic system; do not assume every spell shares the same stats.

quests.title: Experiment with Improvable Skills
quests.description: Use the Improvable Skills guidebook from your Akashic Tome, or locate the guide in JEI if needed. Its ordinary experience-powered perks are separate from Tyz's shared skill points and MXP.

quests.title: Inspect Cooldown and Casting Perks
quests.description: Core Magic is a universal tree, not a specialization choice. Read the Tyz node requirements and effects before investing; potency, resource efficiency, reservoir and recovery only work where a real mod adapter exists. No quest grants a skill bonus.

quests.title: Plan for Practical Attribute Caps
quests.description: Read the configured skill ranks and test actual effects. Individual attributes have their own limits, and cross-mod interactions may differ. This is a reference check, not an attribute grant.

quests.title: Choose One Specialization
quests.description: Core Magic is available to everyone, with Improvable Skills 3 separate. You may remain unspecialized or choose ONE specialization from the same pool: Monk, Hunter, Gilded, Vampire, Werewolf, a Cave/Forest/Sea Dragon, or either Lich route. Human disciplines and supernatural forms are not independent slots. Only explicitly authorized combinations are exceptions: Archlich joins both lich routes; Dracolich joins a dragon and exactly one lich route. Vampire/Werewolf Abomination is an approved planned hybrid, not yet fully implemented. Monk plus any dragon is prohibited. Other planned exceptions are Revenant (Hunter first, then either or both lichdoms), Golden Dragon (Gilded and Cave Dragon, either order), and Blood Immortal (Monk first, then the actual Lilith ritual). Unlisted combinations are not allowed by default. Read freely; checkmarks never enroll you, and the native acquisition/Progression engine enforces eligibility. An additional owner-approved design exception is Piglich: a character must enroll as Gilded first, then obtain either or both lichdoms. A preexisting lich cannot join Gilded. This exception is planned, not currently implemented.

quests.title: Tech Overview: Energy Without a Tech Pack
quests.description: Too Much Magic relies on magical FE sources, not a nuclear tech stack. Draconic Evolution provides an early fuel generator, crystals, storage in its Energy Core, and the high-risk endgame Reactor. Botania Revived's Mana Fluxfield converts mana into FE. Psi and Hex Casting are further candidates pending exact-version verification. No Bigger Reactors, Create, AE2 or general industrial logistics mod is selected.

quests.title: Craft a Draconic Generator
quests.description: Draconic Evolution supplies a basic generator for starting its FE network. This path can be explored independently of nuclear generation; JEI confirms the fuel and exact recipe in this installed build.

quests.title: Craft the Draconic Energy Core
quests.description: Craft the Energy Core block. It is the center of a multiblock FE storage bank, not the unstable power-producing Draconic Reactor Core. Pick a protected site and keep your generation and storage separate.

quests.title: Prepare Energy Core Stabilizers
quests.description: Craft four Energy Core Stabilizers. Arrange them symmetrically in a single plane outside the desired spherical core shell. Larger storage tiers need additional structural blocks; check the in-game Build Guide for each tier.

quests.title: Build Input and Output Pylons
quests.description: Craft two Energy Pylons, one for charging and another for discharge. Link them to the Energy Core as the actual FE input/output interface; configure each direction separately in the installed build.

quests.title: Activate the Draconic Power Bank
quests.description: Assemble the Energy Core and four stabilizers, consult the core's Build Guide and tier controls, activate the completed structure, and configure one pylon as input and another as output. Connect a source and consumer; verify stored FE increases and decreases. Never dismantle a charged core without first checking loss behavior.

quests.title: Route FE with a Crystal
quests.description: Craft a Basic Energy I/O Crystal. Draconic Evolution's crystal networking is the pack's intended FE transfer solution, with relay and wireless variants for more complex layouts. Configure input/output direction before connecting machines.

quests.title: Regulate Power with a Flux Gate
quests.description: Build a Flux Gate for controlled FE throughput. A Draconic Reactor needs controlled power delivery and extraction rather than an unrestricted connection, and its safety should be tested in a disposable world.

quests.title: Acquire the Draconic Reactor Core
quests.description: Craft the Draconic Reactor Core—the high-output, high-risk FE generator. Inspect its *exact installed recipe*: it may require Chaos Shards or other resources that can only be acquired after the Guardian, and this quest does not grant or bypass those materials.
quests.depends: Regulate Power with a Flux Gate

quests.title: Four Reactor Stabilizers
quests.description: Craft four Reactor Stabilizers and arrange them around the Draconic Reactor Core with unobstructed line of sight at the proper spacing for this version. These maintain the containment field; they are *not* Energy Core Stabilizers.

quests.title: Build the Reactor Energy Injector
quests.description: Craft the Reactor Energy Injector and ensure it can continuously supply FE to maintain the containment field during operation. Design independent field-power reserves and a safe shutdown path before attempting a start.

quests.title: Plan Safe Reactor Containment
quests.description: On a disposable world, plan a remote reactor site away from your base and important chunks. Separate high-output extraction from containment-field input, add controlled Flux Gate paths and a sufficient battery buffer. A reactor field collapse or runaway heat can destroy the area; do not treat this as safe baseline generation.

quests.title: Operate a Draconic Reactor Safely
quests.description: Only after the structure and sufficient fuel are assembled: monitor temperature, containment field strength, fuel conversion and energy saturation. Start with conservative settings, verify field power is sustained under peak load, and test emergency shutdown in an expendable world. This checkmark is a *manual safety acknowledgment*; it does not certify actual reactor telemetry.

quests.title: Build a Bookshelf
quests.description: Craft a bookshelf to establish a magical research corner. Bookshelves also appear in early Scriptor Magicae tools. The spellbook and world-specific magical vocabulary must still be acquired or discovered.

quests.title: Iron Is Only the Beginning
quests.description: An iron pickaxe is a baseline, not a finish line. Choose spellcasting, rituals, magical mining, farming or exploration. Basic Progression covers shared goals; Magic chapters cover individual schools. You do not need to master all 25 magical traditions.

quests.title: Find an Everyday Magical Shortcut
quests.description: Look through Tips & Tricks for one practical benefit: Ars Break and Magelight, Scriptor's fuel-free Casting Lectern with Inflame, an Occultism ore crusher, portable crafting, or a broom. Check the costs in JEI and choose the magic that appeals to you.

quests.title: Try a First Spell or Ritual
quests.description: Use any school's introductory magic: cast an Ars spell, perform a first Occultism ritual, make use of EvilCraft blood, try witchcraft, or write a Scriptor spell. This checkmark is manual because there is no honest single automatic criterion shared by all schools.

quests.title: A Little Protection
quests.description: Craft an iron chestplate for dangerous exploring. This is optional: players who prefer farming, research or base magic can progress without rushing combat.

quests.title: Take Your Magic Into the World
quests.description: Explore beyond your base for structures, new biomes and useful materials. Nature's Compass, FTB Chunks, your Trinkets Pouch and the exploration chapters all help. You may also specialize in base building without following every dungeon branch.

quests.title: The Rest of the Pack Is Yours
quests.description: Continue with any of our five categories: Introduction for practical shortcuts and food, Progression for shared milestones, Magic for independent schools, Exploration & Combat for adventure, and Endgame much later. The power chapter already contains all intended technology progression. This finishes orientation, not the game.
quests.depends: Try a First Spell or Ritual

quests.title: Smelt Without Fuel: Scriptor Lectern
quests.description: Scriptor Magicae's Casting Lectern (scriptor:casting_lectern) casts a written Inflame spell automatically. Upstream recipe: three wooden slabs, one bookshelf, purple wool. Inflame consumes smeltable ingredients and creates normal furnace outputs without coal, FE or player mana. Total spell cost limits cadence and complexity (default maximum 25) rather than consuming a resource. You must learn this world's magic vocabulary and prepare a book. Our pinned 2.0.14 build still needs an actual adjacent-chest input/output test; do not promise fully unattended chest smelting until verified.

quests.title: Double Raw Ore: Occultism or Mahou?
quests.description: Occultism's early Foliot Crusher turns supported raw ores into two dusts after its first spirit ritual; confirm that these dusts smelt in our pack. Mahou Tsukai's Mortar and Pestle presently produces two catalyst powders from ingots/gems, NOT two smeltable ingots from one raw ore. Our planned ore/dust unification is separate unfinished compatibility work. The cursed EvilCraft Vengeance Pickaxe boosts mined drops through Fortune instead of doubling furnace input.

quests.title: Need Early Flight? Compare Brooms
quests.description: EvilCraft has a modular blood-powered broom. Hexerei has a different witch's broom. Both offer mobility before finding an Elytra, but have distinct recipes, fuels and handling. Check JEI and the appropriate Magic chapter; don't assume unlimited fuel or identical controls.

quests.title: Vengeance Pickaxe: Fortune with a Price
quests.description: EvilCraft's Vengeance Pickaxe provides unusually high Fortune (often Fortune V) with a dangerous Vengeance curse. Upstream crafting uses diamonds, hardened blood and undead wood. It increases drops from ore mining; it does not automatically smelt ore or mine entire veins. Learn the curse before using it on dangerous expeditions.

quests.title: Welcome to the Magic of Alcohol
quests.description: This chapter teaches three DIFFERENT installed drink systems: Brewin' and Chewin' ferments liquids and foods in a Keg; Cocktails Delight adds spirits and mixed drinks, some conditional on other food mods; Beachparty mixes tropical cocktails at a Palm Bar, with a Mini Fridge for ice. Food & Fishing covers farms and meals, while Advanced Progression covers the vanilla Brewing Stand. No separate brewmaster book is required. Read the branches, then check this orientation quest. Task: manual acknowledgment, not a recipe check.

quests.title: Read the Brewer's In-Game Reference
quests.description: Brewin' and Chewin' has NO physical guidebook. Open Advancements (L by default, or your custom keybinding), find the Brewin' and Chewin' tab marked with a beer icon, and browse its Keg progression. For a Keg item use JEI recipe lookup (R) and usages (U); search 'Keg', 'Fermenting' and 'Keg Pouring'. Cocktails Delight recipes are in JEI, including optional integrations; Beachparty uses JEI's Palm Bar Mixing and Mini Fridge Freezing categories. Task: manual check after you open the references; this does not prove brewing.
quests.depends: Welcome to the Magic of Alcohol

quests.title: Build a Keg
quests.description: The Keg is Brewin' and Chewin's main workstation. In a crafting table put three planks across the bottom, iron ingots at top-left/top-right and center-left/center-right, a plank at top-middle, and a honeycomb at center-middle (recipe pattern i-p-i / i-h-i / p-p-p). Any vanilla plank-tag wood qualifies. Place the Keg in a safe workroom and open its inventory. JEI: brewinandchewin:keg recipe. Task: acquire a Keg; this detects possession, not placement.

quests.title: Make Your Serving Tankards
quests.description: Craft Tankards from planks and iron nuggets: top row plank/empty/plank, middle iron nugget/empty/iron nugget, bottom three planks; one craft yields four Tankards. Place empties in the Keg's finished-fluid serving slot, or use the correct container directly on the Keg, to take brewed drinks. The output preview tells you which container fits. JEI: brewinandchewin:tankard. Task: acquire a Tankard (the recipe produces four).

quests.title: Prime the Keg and Read Its Temperature
quests.description: Open the placed Keg. The top four slots hold ingredients; the separate container slot fills the base-fluid tank with water, honey or milk as the JEI Fermenting recipe requires. A Keg stores up to 1000 mB (one bucket). Temperature comes from the environment/nearby blocks and can determine whether the recipe progresses. Match the recipe's full fluid amount, ingredients and temperature; monitor its progress before serving into the indicated container. Task: manually confirm you saw a fermentation progress indicator. Holding a Keg alone does not count.

quests.title: First Brew: Beer
quests.description: In JEI, select Brewin' and Chewin's Beer Fermenting recipe. One 1000 mB water batch uses wheat dough via the c:foods/dough/wheat tag (NOT just raw wheat), wheat seeds and a brown mushroom; leave the unused fourth ingredient slot empty. Use Farmer's Delight / JEI to craft an accepted dough ingredient. Fill the Keg, adjust temperature if JEI requires it, watch fermentation finish, then fill Tankards. Task: manual check after you actually pour Beer; the quest does not falsely infer brewing from item possession.
quests.depends: Prime the Keg and Read Its Temperature

quests.title: A Honey Mead Batch
quests.description: For a second recipe route, select Mead in JEI's Fermenting recipes: use 1000 mB honey as the base fluid plus wheat, wheat seeds and sweet berries (the fourth ingredient slot is empty). Honey is a FLUID input rather than a sugar substitute; obtain it from supported containers. Confirm the recipe's temperature and pour into its required serving container. Task: manual completion after preparing and serving Mead. This is an optional fermentation specialization, not a gate for other drinks.
quests.depends: Prime the Keg and Read Its Temperature

quests.title: A Keg Makes Food, Too
quests.description: A brewery needn't produce only alcohol. The same Keg ferments cheese and fudge. JEI: Fermenting -> Cocoa Fudge uses 250 mB milk, sugar, and two cocoa beans, and requires temperature 2 in the upstream 1.21.1 recipe. Cheeses have their own serving requirements; when the fluid/output indicator requests Honeycomb, use it rather than a Tankard. See JEI's individual recipes and Farmer's Delight Cutting Board usages for slicing prepared cheese. Task: manual check after successfully producing ONE edible fermented food; optional.
quests.depends: Prime the Keg and Read Its Temperature

quests.title: Transfer a Full Keg
quests.description: A Keg may be carried with liquid still inside, and its capacity is 1000 mB. Use this to move a prepared batch from a brewing shed to a bar. First inspect the stored fluid before breaking or moving it, then place the Keg and confirm its contents remain. Do not assume ingredients or finished servings survive all pickup methods; test safely with an ordinary batch. Task: manual confirmation of successful fluid transport. Optional utility trick.
quests.depends: Prime the Keg and Read Its Temperature

quests.title: Cocktails Delight: Learn the Two Workflows
quests.description: Cocktails Delight EXTENDS the Keg with new fermented spirits and uses ordinary crafting recipes for many mixed cocktails. In JEI, find the Fermenting and Keg Pouring categories for spirits, then press U on the obtained drink item to see its crafting-table cocktail uses. Many drinks work with vanilla and Farmer's Delight; others are conditional on external crop/item tags. Do not assume every advertised drink exists in this pack. Task: manual check after inspecting at least one fermentation and one mixed-drink recipe; optional branch.

quests.title: Ferment White Rum
quests.description: Cocktails Delight's White Rum is brewed in the Brewin' and Chewin' Keg, NOT at Beachparty's Palm Bar. Upstream Fermenting recipe: 1000 mB water, THREE sugar cane and ONE sugar; fermentation time 8400 ticks and required temperature value 4. Check JEI for which conditions achieve that heat in this version. Pour the finished rum using Keg Pouring into the serving item indicated by JEI. Task: acquire cocktailsdelight:rum; an item check does not confirm HOW the drink was brewed. Optional if you prefer the tropical route.
quests.depends: Cocktails Delight: Learn the Two Workflows

quests.title: Mix a Drink and Check Its Side Effects
quests.description: A spirit is usually an INPUT to a cocktail, not the finished mixed drink. Press U on the White Rum or another Cocktails Delight ingredient in JEI and select a recipe available with this pack's crops, bottle count and crafting table. Craft a mixed drink and inspect its tooltip before drinking. Many alcoholic drinks trigger Brewin' and Chewin's Tipsy/Intoxication; some Cocktails Delight recipes grant combat or XP effects. Avoid stacking effects during XP/skill testing until compatibility has been audited. Task: manual completion after mixing one available drink; optional.

quests.title: The Piña Colada Ingredient Puzzle
quests.description: Yes, there IS a Piña Colada item in Cocktails Delight, but its recipe is CONDITIONAL. In JEI search cocktailsdelight:pina_colada. The upstream recipe is shapeless: TWO items under c:foods/pineapple_item, ONE item under c:foods/coconut, ONE White Rum and FOUR glass bottles; it yields four cocktails. It is registered only when BOTH food tags are nonempty. Beachparty coconuts and Pam's crops must actually populate those common tags; do not assume they do. If JEI lacks the recipe, record the missing-tag incompatibility instead of chasing an impossible craft. Task: manual check after verifying the available recipe or identifying the tag gap; optional, NEVER blocks the chapter.
quests.depends: Mix a Drink and Check Its Side Effects

quests.title: Find Coconuts and Palm Wood
quests.description: Beachparty's tropical work starts on a coast with naturally generated palms. Gather Palm Logs and coconuts hanging beneath foliage; turn logs into Palm Planks. Coconuts can be opened for drink ingredients and can help produce palm sprouts on suitable sand. The beach biome and worldgen are a discovery route, not a hard quest lock: bring home saplings if you want a base elsewhere. Use JEI on Palm Planks and Coconut Open. Task: manual check when you have examined a palm and obtained its useful materials.

quests.title: Construct a Palm Bar
quests.description: Beachparty's Palm Bar is a separate cocktail mixer; it does NOT ferment your Keg's spirits. Craft it using SEVEN Palm Planks arranged ### / ##(empty) / ##(empty) in a crafting grid; the recipe yields three Palm Bars. Place one in your bungalow, open it, and inspect JEI's Palm Bar Mixing recipes. Task: acquire beachparty:palm_bar, which detects possession rather than an actual successful cocktail.

quests.title: Build a Mini Fridge for Ice
quests.description: For Beachparty cocktails, the Mini Fridge makes ice without requiring a frozen biome. Craft a Mini Fridge from FIVE iron ingots and ONE redstone (pattern III / IRI), then put a WATER potion bottle in it: the Mini Fridge Freezing recipe produces Ice after 1200 ticks (about a minute). Verify the JEI Freezing recipe and collect the Ice for Palm Bar Mixing. Task: acquire beachparty:mini_fridge; you must separately test that freezing works.

quests.title: Serve a Coconut Cocktail
quests.description: At the Palm Bar, mix ONE Open Coconut (beachparty:coconut_open), ONE block of Ice and ONE Honey Bottle. JEI category: Palm Bar Mixing -> Coconut Cocktail. This makes beachparty:coconut_cocktail, a refreshing tropical drink with a temporary Strength effect. It is DISTINCT from Cocktails Delight's conditional Piña Colada, and does NOT need rum or a Keg. Task: acquire the Coconut Cocktail; possession doesn't verify drinking it.
quests.depends: Build a Mini Fridge for Ice

quests.title: Place, Sip, and Compare Effects
quests.description: Beachparty cocktails are placeable drinks. Set a Coconut Cocktail on a table/counter and interact with it to sip servings; the upstream wiki describes three placed servings (30 seconds each), compared with consuming it directly. Other Palm Bar flavors have their own effects: Sweet Berries (Absorption), Cocoa (Regeneration), Pumpkin (Fire Resistance), Honey (Haste), Melon (Luck). Check the effects and durations in this pinned client. Task: manual check after placing a drink and taking a serving. Optional: do not require alcohol consumption to finish the book.

quests.title: Open the Beach Bungalow
quests.description: Final open-ended build: set up a Palm Bar, Mini Fridge and a stocked Coconut Cocktail table at a coastal bungalow. Optionally include a Keg, Tankards, cheese and a Cocktails Delight mixing area; provide a lounge chair, fishing spot and a safe storage barrel. Aquaculture 2 supplies fishing, Farmer's Delight and Pam's provide food, and Let's Do Furniture supplies extra décor. You do NOT need to craft all 40+ Cocktails Delight recipes or obtain conditional missing ingredients. Task: manual check after your functioning beach bar is assembled; chapter complete!

quests.title: Ars: A Workshop with Teeth
quests.description: Start with a spellbook, build a Source-powered workshop, then challenge the Wilden Chimera and pursue archmage spells. Side branches teach helpers, practical tricks, and all seven installed Ars add-ons. Explore freely; the side branches are optional, and recipes still enforce their own costs.
quests.manual_rationale: Brief initial chapter orientation; no gameplay accomplishment or item payout is claimed.

quests.title: Your First Spellbook
quests.description: Obtain a Novice Spell Book, either by crafting it or choosing it as your starter gift. Open its spell editor and begin with a simple Touch spell before stacking expensive effects. Mana pays for personal casting; Source in jars runs your workshop. Those are different resources.

quests.title: Amethyst Goes In, Source Gems Come Out
quests.description: Craft an Imbuement Chamber and place amethyst or lapis inside to make Source Gems. It can slowly complete basic recipes without a generator; nearby Source accelerates production. For essence recipes, arrange the displayed ingredients on nearby pedestals. Those surrounding ingredients are catalysts, so keep them for the next batch.

quests.title: The Table That Eats Your Homework
quests.description: Craft a Scribe's Table, then use your spellbook on it to choose a glyph. Supply the displayed ingredients and the required experience; learning the resulting glyph expands your spell editor. The table can pull ingredients from nearby inventories. A Dominion Wand can disable that behavior when your storage starts volunteering valuables.

quests.title: Bottle the Workshop Budget
quests.description: Craft a Source Jar before expecting a Sourcelink to power your machines. Jars store Source, rather than your personal casting mana. Keep the first jar close to both your generator and its consumers, and watch its fill level while you work. An empty jar is an attractive explanation for a stalled recipe.
quests.depends: Amethyst Goes In, Source Gems Come Out

quests.title: Your Garden Has a Second Job
quests.description: Craft an Agronomic Sourcelink and place it near growing crops or trees, with a Source Jar nearby. Natural growth generates Source; magical plants receive bonuses. Bone meal does not directly earn Source from this link, so use the reward to establish the garden rather than expecting a perpetual bone-meal power station.

quests.title: Link Direction Is a Verb
quests.description: Craft a Source Relay to move energy beyond a single workbench. With a Dominion Wand, select the jar first and the relay second to draw Source; select the relay first and a destination jar second to deliver it. Redstone disables a relay. This is useful when your factory needs an actual off switch.

quests.title: Eight Pedestals and a Plan
quests.description: Craft an Enchanting Apparatus and give it an Arcane Core at its base. Arrange Arcane Pedestals within three blocks, load the recipe's surrounding ingredients, then use its central reagent on the apparatus. Supply Source when the recipe requests it. The reward covers the pedestal ring; it does not replace the core or the ingredients.
quests.depends: Amethyst Goes In, Source Gems Come Out

quests.title: Grow Your Own Wardrobe
quests.description: Obtain Magebloom Seeds through the apparatus recipe, then grow a renewable supply. Magebloom becomes fiber for magical clothing and also contributes to an Agronomic Sourcelink's garden. Reserve some harvest for crafting before feeding everything into another machine. A wizard whose shirt was eaten by the power plant has made a planning error.

quests.title: The Mage Upgrade
quests.description: Upgrade your Novice Spell Book to the Mage's Spell Book, whose registry name still says apprentice. This unlocks the second spell tier and more room for combinations. Upgrade the existing book so your work travels with you. Your next experiments can include mobility and automation, rather than simply making every projectile more expensive.

quests.title: Rituals Need Floor Space
quests.description: Craft a Ritual Brazier and leave working space around it. Insert the desired tablet, supply any required augments, and activate with an empty hand. Read the ritual's Source requirements before lighting it. Different rituals have different effects and costs; a decorative brazier on the bookshelf is a poor place to discover that distinction.

quests.title: Schedule a Very Bad Meeting
quests.description: Craft the Tablet of Summon Wilden, then prepare a separate arena away from your workshop. Unaugmented, it summons ordinary Wilden. To call the Chimera, augment the ritual with a Wilden Spike, Horn, and Wing before activating it. The Chimera summon destroys nearby blocks, so keep your storage, home, and other players' builds out of the clearing. Bring armor, reliable damage, food, and a way to recover from movement mistakes. Merely making the tablet completes this preparation quest; the next quest requires a credited kill.

quests.title: The Meeting Has Escalated
quests.description: Defeat a Wilden Chimera with a player-credited kill. Keep moving through its changing attacks, and collect the Wilden Tribute before leaving the arena. This quest detects the kill itself; buying or borrowing a Tribute does not substitute. Your commemorative soundtrack is considerably less destructive than the performance you just attended.

quests.title: Archmage, Pending Paperwork
quests.description: Upgrade your Mage's Spell Book to an Archmage Spell Book to unlock the highest native spell tier. The recipe also demands a Wilden Tribute, Nether Star, Totem, and other valuables; winning the Chimera fight is only part of the bill. The Spell Power thread is a finishing gift for your existing armor, not a substitute for its upgrades.

quests.title: Robes with Actual Benefits
quests.description: Craft Arcanist's Robes as your entry into Ars magical armor. Armor families trade protection against their thread-slot arrangements, so compare them before committing resources to a full set. Upgrade recipes and enchanting matter too. The dye is for professional credibility; enemies remain unconvinced by academic dress alone.

quests.title: Read the Slot Before Sewing
quests.description: Craft an Alteration Table to manage armor threads. Match each thread to a slot that supports its required level; some effects only work in a level-three slot. Thread of Gliding is a particularly useful later target. Owning a thread and wearing armor are not enough if you have stitched it into the wrong slot.

quests.title: Hire a Small Orange Courier
quests.description: Obtain a Starbuncle Charm, then use it to establish your first item-carrying helper. Use the Dominion Wand to assign inventories and test a short route before building a complicated factory. Keep walkable paths between its jobs. The sunglasses are compensation for being asked to carry your entire magical career one stack at a time.

quests.title: A Gardener with Standards
quests.description: Obtain a Whirlisprig Charm and read its garden requirements before setting up production. Give the helper a varied, suitable environment and Source, rather than an empty box with one miserable plant. Observe the output before expanding. The reward helps decorate its workplace; job satisfaction is unusually literal in this branch of horticulture.

quests.title: Loot without the Assembly Line
quests.description: Obtain a Drygmy Charm, then build its henge and supply Source near suitable creatures. Drygmy automation can generate drops without repeatedly killing its neighbors. More setup and creature variety matter; it is not a promise that every boss or special drop is eligible. Test ordinary mobs before designing your retirement around a rare loot table.

quests.title: A Witch with a Work Order
quests.description: Obtain a Wixie Charm to start investigating potion and crafting automation. Consult its notebook entry for the correct base block and workstation setup, then provide reachable ingredients and Source. Test a single recipe before scaling. The reward starts a potion ingredient reserve; it does not persuade a Wixie to work without the rest of its recipe.

quests.title: Promote a Helper to Familiar
quests.description: Use the Ritual of Binding with an eligible Ars creature to unlock a familiar, then select it through your spellbook's familiar controls. A working helper and a summoned familiar serve different roles. This quest waits for Ars's familiar-unlock advancement, so merely carrying a charm does not count. Celebrate with pie before assigning another shift.

quests.title: A Spell with a Day Job
quests.description: Obtain a Basic Spell Turret, inscribe a simple spell, and provide Source plus a redstone trigger. A light or crop utility spell makes a better first test than uncontrolled explosions. Verify its aim and cost before giving it a repeating signal. The daylight detector offers a practical scheduling option once the spell behaves.

quests.title: Craft from a Magical Library
quests.description: Craft a Storage Lectern to browse and craft from linked inventories. Connect inventory to lectern with the Dominion Wand and add Bookwyrms when you need more connections. Name storage clearly so future searches make sense. This is Ars's storage lectern, distinct from both the ordinary lectern and Scriptor's fuel-free Casting Lectern.

quests.title: Give the Library a Catalog
quests.description: Craft a Repository as compact storage for your magical library. Naming repositories makes their tabs easier to recognize, while a Repository Catalog can proxy a connected chain for the lectern. Read filter behavior before connecting automated input. The name tags are an invitation to improve your filing system, not to label every chest Miscellaneous Two.

quests.title: Leave Yourself a Way Home
quests.description: Obtain a Warp Scroll and bind a safe destination before taking it exploring. Scrolls also participate in Ars portal building; read the notebook's frame and activation instructions for that route. Mark the destination clearly and test it before relying on a desperate escape. A return address inside a wall is still an address.

quests.title: Creative Flight, Local Subscription
quests.description: Craft the Tablet of Flight for Source-powered work around a base. Its ritual refreshes nearby players' temporary flight buff when they jump; leaving the ritual area or exhausting Source ends that convenience. Build a safe landing area and test the range close to the ground. This is excellent construction infrastructure, but it is not permanent global flight.

quests.title: Put an Emergency Spell in Your Pocket
quests.description: Craft an Enchanter's Mirror and inscribe a useful self-targeted spell at the Scribe's Table. Slowfall is a good safety experiment once learned, particularly before testing Launch movement. Select the intended spell before inscribing and test at a safe height. A beautifully copied attack spell is not a parachute.

quests.title: A Potion for More than One Occasion
quests.description: Obtain a Potion Flask to investigate reusable potion storage rather than carrying a bag of individual drinks. Use the Ars notebook's filling instructions and compare the extended or amplified flask upgrades later. Keep a reliable healing or utility supply for rituals and boss attempts. The reward supplies brewing ingredients; it does not fill the flask automatically.

quests.title: An Amethyst Department
quests.description: Obtain an Amethyst Golem Charm and investigate its amethyst-farming role around a geode. Preserve your budding amethyst and give the helper suitable access rather than mining the productive blocks away. This pairs naturally with Source Gem production. The calcite is decorative compensation for turning a geological discovery into another department.

quests.title: Additions: Bulk Linking, Fewer Clicks
quests.description: Craft an Advanced Dominion Wand for configurable link order and bulk selection. Use its radial controls to choose first or second endpoint and single or multiple targets. In multi mode, crouch-use can find connected matching blocks. Test on a small row first; a convenient bulk tool also makes it convenient to misunderstand a whole row at once.

quests.title: Additions: The Library Travels with You
quests.description: Craft a Warp Index and link it to your Storage Lectern for remote inventory access in the same dimension. The lectern must remain chunk-loaded; distance access does not keep your base running. The Stabilized Warp Index extends access across dimensions. Label the destination and verify a small withdrawal before leaving your entire expedition kit in remote storage.

quests.title: Additions: Source on the Other End
quests.description: Craft an Ender Source Jar to investigate its shared Source pool across placed jars. Supply generation at your base, keep the relevant areas loaded, and compare a consumer's behavior before and after connecting it. Shared storage moves your Source budget; it does not multiply production. The reward helps fund more spatially questionable workshop experiments.
quests.depends: Additions: The Library Travels with You

quests.title: Controle: Configure from a Distance
quests.description: Craft Controle's Remote for Dominion-Wand-compatible configuration. Crouch-use a target, then choose endpoint locking and single or multiple selection with its radial controls. For example, locking a Storage Lectern as the last endpoint simplifies inventory linking. Clear the stored target when finished. The Remote reports invalid or cross-dimension targets rather than making every connection possible.

quests.title: Controle: Give the Farm an Off Switch
quests.description: Craft a Temporal Stability Sensor and read it with a comparator. Higher output indicates the world is closer to lagging; use that signal to stop optional automation before it overwhelms the server. Start with a reversible farm cutoff and test both states. This is a control signal, not a machine that removes lag by existing nearby.

quests.title: Controle: A Ritual That Follows You
quests.description: Craft a Portable Brazier Relay to investigate carrying supported ritual effects with you. The original brazier must stay loaded and supplied with Source, and some rituals are blacklisted. Start with a safe utility ritual and verify its behavior near the base before traveling. Portability relocates the benefit; it does not make the original ritual self-sufficient.

quests.title: Elemental: Choose an Element, Keep Options
quests.description: Create a Lesser Fire Focus in the Imbuement Chamber as an introduction to elemental specialization. Read the focus's bonuses and its penalties to other schools before equipping it. Upgrading to the major focus is a later project. This fire example does not lock your character into fire; other elemental foci remain available when your spell designs change.

quests.title: Elemental: Source-Powered Plumbing
quests.description: Craft an Urn of Endless Waters and link a supported destination with a Dominion Wand. It converts Source into water for containers such as cauldrons and Botania's Apothecary. Supply Source and check the destination before expanding. The reward gives it an immediate job, and establishes that even an endless urn can have a utility bill.
quests.depends: Elemental: Choose an Element, Keep Options

quests.title: Elemental: Dress for Your School
quests.description: Craft a Pyromancer's Hat as a first elemental armor upgrade. Compare its school benefits, thread slots, and full-set conditions with your current armor before replacing every piece. The recipe's actual armor tier matters, so inspect it in JEI. You may pursue the water, air, or earth counterparts independently; this quest uses fire as a worked example.
quests.depends: Elemental: Choose an Element, Keep Options

quests.title: Elemancy: Fire Meets Air
quests.description: Make Cinder Essence by imbuing Manipulation Essence with Fire and Air Essences on the surrounding pedestals. This introduces Elemancy's combined-school crafting without asking you to memorize every combination. The surrounding catalysts stay in place during imbuement; keep them for another batch. Cinder is the fire-and-air route, while other pairings have their own essences and armor.

quests.title: Elemancy: Two Schools, One Hat
quests.description: Craft a Cindermancer Hat through Elemancy's upgraded armor route. Its fire-and-air identity builds on elemental specialization; compare the actual recipe and set conditions before converting your favorite armor. Inspect retained threads and enchantments after upgrading. The reward is a small supply of literal firepower, because apparently the combined-school hat was not sufficient warning.

quests.title: Ocultas: Attunement without a Diamond
quests.description: Obtain a Spirit Attuned Gem. Ars Ocultas offers an Enchanting Apparatus route using a Source Gem, Conjuration Essence, Manipulation Essence, and Demon's Dream Essence, plus Source. Check JEI against your available ingredients. This inventory objective accepts a gem from either valid route; it teaches an alternative when diamonds are scarce without pretending to identify how you crafted it.

quests.title: Ocultas: Prepare a Spirit Office
quests.description: Obtain a Containment Jar, then investigate placing a summoned Occultism worker spirit inside through Ars containment. Jarred spirits retain their normal jobs without expiring, and accept suitable nearby items or hopper input. A crusher still needs output collection. This task detects the jar as equipment; trapping and testing a worker are the practical next steps, not an implied completed automation.

quests.title: Ocultas: The Sacrifice Has Been Delegated
quests.description: Craft the Sacrificial Altar through Ars Ocultas's apparatus recipe. Its integration supports Occultism ritual work involving nearby contained creatures and supplied items. Follow the installed recipe and test with an ordinary eligible ritual before trusting valuable summons to the arrangement. Acquiring the altar is the milestone here; it does not prove a ritual ran or waive its native requirements.

quests.title: Ars 'n Spells: Build the Spell Loom
quests.description: Build a Spell Loom to carry an Ars spell into Iron's Spellbooks. Select the desired spell in a reusable Ars book, place it in the source slot, and supply a blank scroll. Names, backgrounds, and icons help identify the result; they do not change its school or cost. A filled Iron's scroll is not a blank target.

quests.title: Ars 'n Spells: Weave a Carrier Scroll
quests.description: Use the Spell Loom to inscribe an Ars spell onto a blank target scroll. A reusable book or focus stays intact; a disposable parchment costs one unit. Clear the output slot before another inscription. This quest uses the add-on's transcription advancement, so owning a Loom alone is insufficient. Avoid Convert unless you intend to erase an existing spell.
quests.depends: Ars 'n Spells: Build the Spell Loom

quests.title: Ars 'n Spells: Bind It into the Wheel
quests.description: Bind your inscribed carrier scroll into a real Iron's spellbook at its Inscription Table, or use the Spellbook Binding ritual. For that ritual, leave exactly one carrier and one book within three blocks, with no other dropped items, then activate the brazier empty-handed. Binding consumes the carrier and adds a spell-wheel entry; a full or duplicate book can refuse it.
quests.depends: Ars 'n Spells: Weave a Carrier Scroll

quests.title: Ars 'n Spells: Cast across the Curriculum
quests.description: Select the bound Ars entry in Iron's native spell wheel and successfully cast it. This quest waits for the add-on's cross-cast advancement. Watch the shared mana payment and begin with a cheap harmless spell; cross-casting can add overhead and follows server resource settings. Having two casting interfaces is not permission to spend the same mana twice.
quests.depends: Ars 'n Spells: Bind It into the Wheel

quests.title: Unification: A Knife Made of Magic
quests.description: Collect four Pumpkin Slices. Ars Unification imports supported Farmer's Delight cutting recipes into the Cut glyph: try Touch, Cut, Sensitive on a dropped pumpkin, and inspect the Cut category in JEI. Keep the experiment away from valuables. This collection task accepts slices from any valid preparation method; it introduces the magical route without claiming to track which tool made them.

quests.title: Unification: Prep More, Chase Less
quests.description: Collect eight Cabbage Leaves, trying the imported Cut recipe on dropped cabbages. Sensitive enables nearby-item processing; AoE expands the search and Pierce increases how many items Cut processes. Test a small stack and collect its output before automating. The leaves are inventory-detected regardless of preparation method. Only installed integrations contribute recipes; an add-on is not a promise of every machine from absent mods.
quests.depends: Unification: A Knife Made of Magic

quests.title: The Monk Path
quests.description: This is one of the mutually exclusive specialization choices, not a second class or species slot. Monks cultivate unarmed combat, movement and survival through class trials. Consult the Monk path in the skill interface and follow its current initiation requirements; the intended sunset initiation and reserved fist slot are subject to the integrated path data. Claiming this guide does not enroll you.

quests.title: The Hunter Path
quests.description: This is one of the mutually exclusive specialization choices, not a second class or species slot. Hunters specialize against creature families and gain progression through qualifying kills. The intended initiation uses poison while regeneration is active; follow the current path requirements and then choose a specialization. Mutagenic Brews and permanent mutations are separate progression milestones; verify implemented recipes and effects in JEI. This guide does not enroll you.

quests.title: The Gilded Path
quests.description: This is one of the mutually exclusive specialization choices, not a second class or species slot. Gilded is a planned TMM character path using the shared Progression engine. Inspect the available path definitions in your build. If no Gilded enrollment or tree is exposed, it is not yet available; this guide does not imply any implemented requirements or powers. Gilded-first lichdom (Piglich) is an approved future exception: enroll as Gilded before acquiring one or both native lich forms. Existing liches cannot enroll retroactively. Runtime implementation and testing are pending.

quests.title: Becoming a Vampire
quests.description: This is one of the mutually exclusive specialization choices, not a second class or species slot. JAWR owns vampirism in this pack; the separate Vampirism mod is retired. Consult JAWR's in-game guide for the native transformation and Lilith's blood route; inspect the Vampire skill category after successful transformation. Blood feeding and sunlight are native mechanics. This checkmark does not change your form.

quests.title: Becoming a Werewolf
quests.description: This is one of the mutually exclusive specialization choices, not a second class or species slot. JAWR also owns lycanthropy; the separate Werewolves mod is retired. Consult the JAWR in-game guide and its wolfsbane-related transformation route, then inspect the Werewolf skill category. Follow the current native cure rules before changing forms. This checkmark is not a transformation trigger.

quests.title: Becoming a Dragon
quests.description: This is one of the mutually exclusive specialization choices, not a second class or species slot. Dragon Survival provides Cave, Forest and Sea dragon forms with different diets and abilities. Open its native species selection interface when installed and eligible; consult the current controls and diet tooltips before choosing. TMM's diet and form compatibility are subject to live testing. This quest is an informational guide, not a species setter.

quests.title: Lichdom: Forbidden Magic
quests.description: This is one of the mutually exclusive specialization choices, not a second class or species slot. JAWR: Forbidden Magic provides its own lich path and phylactery. Use the mod's guide for the native ritual, soul storage, resurrection anchor and cure; check the corresponding Tyz category after transformation where implemented. This guide does not grant lichdom or create a resurrection anchor.

quests.title: Lichdom: Goety
quests.description: This is one of the mutually exclusive specialization choices, not a second class or species slot. Goety offers a distinct lich path. Follow the native guide's lich ritual and prepare the Arca for native soul storage and resurrection. The Goety chapter owns its general ritual and summoning progression; character form guidance lives here. No transformation is granted by this quest.

quests.title: The Archlich
quests.description: This is an explicit exception to the one-specialization rule, not a separate slot or permission to combine arbitrary paths. The intended Archlich combines the two distinct lich paths, with JAWR phylactery-first resurrection and Goety Arca fallback. This compatibility is experimental; do not treat it as a third independent lich source or assume untested death behavior. No transformation or resurrection is granted here. A Gilded-first character may also acquire both lich forms as a Piglich. That additional exception is approved design only; the runtime enrollment policy must be extended and tested.

quests.title: The Dracolich
quests.description: This is an explicit exception to the one-specialization rule, not a separate slot or permission to combine arbitrary paths. The intended Dracolich combines one Dragon Survival form with exactly one lich source, not both. Dragon growth and the chosen native resurrection anchor should be retained. The integration is experimental; confirm current build support before attempting it. This guide cannot change species or create an anchor.

quests.title: Relics: Learn Your Relic
quests.description: Discover Relics equipment, read its ability and condition tooltips and equip it in the appropriate Curios slot. Inspect its own progression interface before spending upgrades. Relics belongs in this chapter alongside Artifacts; this checkmark does not grant equipment or rank.

quests.title: Reliquified Artifacts
quests.description: Reliquified Artifacts integrates Artifacts equipment with Relics-style progression, including item-specific XP, ranks and durability where supported. Inspect the actual item tooltip and progression interface; do not assume all accessories use identical triggers. This is orientation, not an automatic rank or repair.

quests.title: ProjectE Energy Converters
quests.description: ProjectE Energy Converters bridges EMC with FE and supported energy systems. Find its conversion blocks through JEI when available; follow the actual ProjectE and Project Expansion recipe gates and check the configured conversion ratios before use. This guide grants no converter and does not bypass any gate.

quests.title: Hermetica: Your Alchemical Field Guide
quests.description: Craft the Hermetica guide with a Book and two accepted sand-tag items. Open Getting Started and Spagyrics: Theurgy separates heat, Mercury, Salt, Sulfur, and fluid Sal Ammoniac. Identify each before buying machinery. Check this orientation when you have located those pages. This is a manual reading acknowledgement, not a detector for opening the guide. You are free to explore other schools afterward.

quests.title: Light a Pyromantic Brazier
quests.description: Craft a Pyromantic Brazier and place it beneath a Theurgy machine with a heat receiver. Supply ordinary furnace fuel. This supplies Theurgy heat, not Forge Energy or Mercury Flux. In Hermetica, use Getting Started and Spagyrics' heat instructions to check spacing and accepted fuels. Task: possess the Brazier; FTB does not verify that a machine has heated up.

quests.title: Distill Mercury from Stone
quests.description: Craft a Mercury Distiller and place it over a working heat source. In Hermetica or JEI, find Distillation and feed a supported material: the tagged-release default example uses ten stone-tag blocks or fifteen sand-tag items for one Mercury Shard. Collect the output. The quest detects the Distiller item, not successful Mercury production; consult JEI in the installed pack for the effective recipe.

quests.title: Calcine the Four Salt Families
quests.description: Build and heat a Calcination Oven. Compare stone to Strata Salt, tagged ores/raw materials to Mineral Salt, plants to Plant Salt and eligible creature materials to Creature Salt in JEI/Spagyrics. The tagged source example grants three Mineral Salt for a qualifying ore; this is not a promise of universal ore doubling. Task: acquire the oven. Check a real output in-game yourself.

quests.title: Collect Sal Ammoniac
quests.description: Craft a Sal Ammoniac Accumulator and its Tank, connect the tank as Hermetica shows, and supply water. The tagged-source baseline converts 1000 mB Water to 100 mB Sal Ammoniac without crystal assistance. A crystal-assisted recipe yields more but its exact reuse behavior needs runtime verification. Use the fluid gauges; owning an Accumulator does not establish that fluid was generated.

quests.title: Liquefy a Material into Sulfur
quests.description: Make and heat a Liquefaction Cauldron. Supply stored Sal Ammoniac and an eligible source—an Oak Log is a useful beginner example—and retrieve its identity-specific Alchemical Sulfur. Check Liquefaction in JEI and Hermetica for the amount; many ordinary logs use 10 mB in tagged source. This is not generic Sulfur interchangeable between all targets. Quest task checks acquisition of the cauldron, not that liquefaction happened.

quests.title: Assemble the Three-Vessel Incubator
quests.description: Craft the two-block Incubator and its Mercury, Salt and Sulfur vessels. Place the three named vessels adjacent to the Incubator's lower block, with effective heat beneath; use Hermetica's Incubation layout instead of assuming the decorative shape is enough. Fill each vessel with its own material class. The task detects an Incubator item only; placement, correct adjacency and heating must be checked in-world.

quests.title: Incubate an Oak Log
quests.description: Use the three vessels with a Mercury Shard, Plant Salt and the Alchemical Sulfur made from an Oak Log. Run the heated Incubator and collect the Oak Log from its output. The tagged-release example takes 100 ticks, but your installed JEI/Hermetica is authoritative. This manual checkmark is an honest observation of your first recreation, not proof supplied by FTB. You now know a complete Theurgy production loop.

quests.title: Repeat with Another Material
quests.description: Choose a second eligible material in JEI. Work backward from its Incubation recipe to the correct Salt class, source-specific Sulfur, Mercury and heat. Build only the missing components and observe the real output. Materials such as logs, ores and animal drops have different valid recipes and costs. Manually check this after completing a second loop; an ordinary inventory possession task cannot prove which workstation produced an item.

quests.title: Ferment Your First Niter
quests.description: Craft a Fermentation Vat. Use its JEI/Hermetica recipe with an eligible Alchemical Sulfur, organic starter/crop/seed/sugar material and the correct Water amount. The tagged-release recipes vary from 125 to 1000 mB; the output is a material-family Niter, not a free universal substance. The item task checks the Vat, not an actual completed fermentation batch.

quests.title: Digest Gold for Reagents
quests.description: Craft a Digestion Vat. In JEI, inspect the Purified Gold recipe: tagged-release source uses a Gold Ingot, compatible Alchemical Salt and 1000 mB Water for twenty Purified Gold. Operate the machine and collect output; the item task verifies possession of the vat, not its operation. Pay attention to the Vat's open/closed state when you later automate it.

quests.title: Exalt Niter, Not Your Tool Tier
quests.description: Use a matching Niter family and Purified Gold to perform one legal Digestion rank upgrade. The common early source ratio is four lower-rank Niter to one higher-rank Niter with Sal Ammoniac; mob families and higher ranks can cost more. Abundant, Common, Rare and Precious are Niter categories, not the Stone/Iron/Diamond/Netherite divination-rod levels. Checkmark is manual: verify the real resulting Niter yourself.

quests.title: Build a Mercury Flux Supply
quests.description: Build the Mercury Catalyst and use a Mercury Shard to fill its independent Mercury Flux store; tagged-release source converts one shard to 800 Mercury Flux. This is not Forge Energy and cannot be assumed compatible with Draconic energy machinery. Study Hermetica's Reformation apparatus and JEI before building the Sulfuric Flux Emitter and its three pedestal roles. The item task proves you acquired the catalyst, not a measured Flux transfer.

quests.title: Reform with a Real Target Sample
quests.description: Build the Sulfuric Flux Emitter and separate Source, Target and Result Pedestals. Place a real pre-existing target Alchemical Sulfur or Niter in the Target Pedestal, compatible source reagents in Source, and supply sufficient Mercury Flux; collect an eligible result. Tagged source pricing varies by tier (50/100/150/200 Flux). The target sample is retained, but must exist first. This quest only detects possession of the Target Pedestal; it does not certify successful Reformation.
prerequisites: Exalt Niter, Not Your Tool Tier

quests.title: Scan with a Basic Divination Rod
quests.description: Craft the Stone-tier Divination Rod and use it on an allowed target. Consult Hermetica's Divination section for target tags and how scan results are shown. The tagged-source baseline describes a 96-block scan range and 40-tick duration; loaded configuration may differ. Possessing the rod is the FTB task; observing an actual scan is separate.

quests.title: Upgrade Your Divination
quests.description: Upgrade to the Iron-tier Divination Rod and perform a scan against an eligible material. Compare Diamond and Netherite tiers and the specialized sulfur-attuned or Amethyst rods in JEI; those are separate tool categories, not Niter upgrades. The quest requires a Tier 2 rod item; higher and specialized models are optional follow-up exploration. It does not detect a successful scan.
quests.depends: Scan with a Basic Divination Rod
prerequisites: Scan with a Basic Divination Rod

quests.title: Heat with a Caloric Flux Emitter
quests.description: Craft a Caloric Flux Emitter, select a legitimate heat-receiving Theurgy machine, supply its own Mercury Flux and observe heating without an ordinary Brazier fuel stack. The source uses 100 Flux per heating operation; follow Hermetica for target selection and range. The emitter provides Theurgy heat, not a generic FE energy grid. This item task verifies you obtained the emitter, not its action.

quests.title: Move Items with Mercurial Wiring
quests.description: Craft a Mercurial Wand, Copper Wire, connection node and Item Extractor/Inserter. Use the Wand to set matching frequency, modes and sides, then move an item between machine inventories that actually expose the required capabilities. See Hermetica's Logistics section. The item task recognizes the Extractor only; it does not prove a successful transfer, infinite throughput or chunk loading.

quests.title: Route Fluids Without Pretending They Are Items
quests.description: Craft Fluid Extractor and Inserter connectors and attach them to suitable Sal Ammoniac or Water tanks. Configure sides, frequency and any supported filters with the Mercurial Wand, then verify that actual fluid—not inventory item stacks—travels. Theurgy's native fluid routing is distinct from its item connectors and does not imply FE support. Quest task detects the Fluid Inserter item; verify transfer independently.

quests.title: Rare Materials: Templates Before Replication
prerequisites: Reform with a Real Target Sample
quests.description: This optional knowledge milestone explains a real safety boundary, not a required Nether Star or Dragon Egg kill. First acquire the original boss item legitimately. Liquefy it with 100 mB Sal Ammoniac to make its named Sulfur and retain a sample on the Reformation Target Pedestal. Tagged source requires two Precious Mob Niter and 200 Mercury Flux for a new Star Sulfur, or four and 200 for an Egg; then Incubate with Creature Salt and Mercury Shard. The physical sample is mandatory: Theurgy cannot conjure a first boss item without it through this chain. Check after reviewing the applicable JEI recipe and sample-gating rule; no boss item is rewarded.
